analysis.title: Europe Open - Measured approach
key_insights: FOMC held rates in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Warsh said he does not think the economy is running hot, which pushed USTs higher.

Fed reducing 'live' meetings to 7 next year and 6 in 2028, which Citi Economics says limits the scope for rate hikes. Citi still expects a Dec hike but says no further hikes this cycle would not be too surprising if risk-off developments continue.
Post-FOMC moves are modest. USTs are still modestly higher but momentum has stalled. Desk flows show better selling in the long end and better buying in the intermediates.
RBNZ Governor Breman said a Dec hike is highly likely. This matches market pricing, so the rates reaction was muted. Antipodeans are catching up to the UST rally.
JGBs are slightly weaker, but Citi's macro strategist still likes long 30y JGBs.
Tech earnings are mixed. Alphabet missed on Q3 revenue and fell as much as 10% pre-market, Samsung also missed, and Microsoft beat. Kospi is down 2% and Nasdaq futures are down 1%.
Amazon and Intel report tonight among a heavy earnings slate, which Citi expects to keep price action choppy.

ECB is widely expected to hold. Focus is on Lagarde's comments on French fiscal strain and ECB intervention tools. Any support is likely to be rhetorical, and Citi expects limited policy guidance with a Dec hike still on track.

ECB spread volatility is reaching a tipping point that could lead markets to price a lower probability of hikes despite rising energy prices. Citi strategists like receiving Dec26 ECB €STR in that scenario.

US data dump at 13:30 GMT: core PCE, advance Q3 GDP, personal income and spending, and jobless claims, plus a 7y auction. Citi economists expect core PCE at 0.31% MoM, supercore at 0.35%, and Q3 GDP at 3.1% on AI capex. Markets are likely more sensitive to growth downside surprises than PCE details.

FX majors held ranges after FOMC, with EURUSD at 1.1138 and 158 capping USDJPY. Interbank volumes were 6% above the 30-day average, with more interest in Asia pairs such as USDCNH (+60%) and USDSGD. Citi remains biased short EUR via crosses and short USDJPY.

Oil is slightly lower on net positive geopolitical headlines. Iran's Supreme Leader reiterated conditions for ending the war, FM Araghchi said Tehran continues to give diplomacy a chance, and WSJ reported VP Vance sent Iran a letter on a peace framework at Trump's direction.

Citi Global Commodities sees a deal by yearend as its central case, but Israeli political gridlock and US midterms make the oil outlook more binary. It sees a higher probability of a more volatile and disruptive oil path.
Sweden Q3 GDP printed 2.1% YoY / 0.4% QoQ vs 3.5% / 1.4% prior. Citi says the Riksbank is unlikely to hike in Nov, and a Dec hike remains plausible depending on inflation.

Israel's election is heading to deadlock. Netanyahu's coalition is projected at 53 seats vs 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, and two Israeli Arab parties doubled to 19 seats. 61 are needed for a majority, and Netanyahu remains in power as coalition talks begin.
Citi FX strategy favors EURNOK as its preferred bearish-EUR vehicle, which should benefit from a US/Iran re-escalation. It remains bearish EUR vs AUD, GBP and CHF.
EM central banks: NBU expected to hike 50bp to 16.50% (third hike in a row, CPI at 10% in September). Egypt expected to hold at 19%.
Citi's chart of the day notes the large compression in term premium makes its US rates strategy hesitant to extend duration beyond the UST front end.
